messages:
Marta T: quick sync — before I hand off tomorrow morning, can we confirm the boundary between SRE vs Runtime oncall? want to avoid any confusion during the holiday burst :wave:
Liam S: good call. short version: SRE = infra/cluster/monitoring/alerts. Runtime = model-serving, fallbacks, model-level regressions and serving bugs.
Raj P: adding escalation paths: SRE escalates to infra-eng (pagerduty infra-p1) for hardware/network; Runtime escalates to runtime-eng and ML research for model regressions.
Ashley C: can we define what we call an "incident"? some of the alerts are noisy and people start paging for non-incidents.
Liam S: agreed. proposed defs: S0/S1 = customer-impacting outage (SLA breach, total service down, data loss). S2 = degraded latency/throughput that impacts a subset of customers. S3 = internal alerts or non-urgent perf regressions.
Marta T: examples help: if GPUs are unreachable -> SRE owns (node failure). if model starts returning nonsense across many requests -> Runtime (model logic / tokenizer / weights). if latency spikes due to overloaded LB -> SRE first.
SRE-Lead: also note combined cases: eg model regression + scale issue — runtime owns the root cause, SRE owns mitigation (add capacity, route traffic). runbook should reflect joint playbook.
oncall-bot: Reminder: oncall rotation swap for 2024-05-02 posted.
Raj P: handoff checklist I left in the rotation doc (links below). key items I keep: current P1s, recent deploys (last 24h), any long-running canaries, upcoming maintenance windows, outstanding runbook TODOs, active experiment flags, contact for GPU vendor.
Marta T: dropping the short handoff notes here:
- current P0: none
- active P1: rolling OOMs on cluster-a (ticket #2342) -> SRE is tracking, mitigation: cordon node pool-b, autoscale turned up
- model alert: drifting eval scores on embedder-v3 (runtime to own investigation)
- infra deploy in progress: kernel upgrade on gpunode-12 (scheduled 02:00 UTC)
- expected traffic spike Friday 18:00 UTC due to partner test
- oncall escalation matrix: 1) try pagerduty group -> 2) ping Slack #eng-oncall -> 3) call SRE-Lead or Runtime-Lead phone
Liam S: tiny addition — for runtime issues, page the runtime team first, but if it's resource-related also page SRE in parallel (use `@sre` and `@runtime` PD routes).
Ashley C: can someone paste the two runbook links?
Marta T: links: https://confluence/redwood/oncall-runbook and https://confluence/redwood/runtime-troubleshooting
Raj P: I pasted a short command to check GPU node health in the runbook — nuked here for quick access:
```
# quick node health
kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpunode
nvidia-smi -L
kubectl top nodes
```
Liam S: also note acceptance criteria for paging S1: confirmed customer error rate > 5% OR average tail latency > 2x baseline for > 5 minutes. add to runbook.
SRE-Lead: final notes for handoff: 1) keep an eye on the OOM mitigation, 2) if you escalate to vendor, tag finance & support, 3) document any deviation from playbook in the ticket.
Marta T: thanks — i'll add these to the handoff doc and do a 10-min live pass with tomorrow's oncall at 09:50 UTC. ping me if any clarifications. :thumbsup:
Ashley C: ack, will join.
oncall-bot: Marta T accepted the handoff task.
